描述_EN: by the tang dynasty (618-906 ad), from which this textile dates, there were a thousand caves decorated with religious scenes. this shrine site is one of china's great buddhist pilgrimage complexes and is situated near the oasis town of dunhuang. the site is also part of an area of central asia we now call the silk road and it refers to a series of overland trade routes that crossed asia from china to europe. the insides of each cave-shrine were painted with coloured murals, some of which survive to this day. most of the textiles from the mogao caves would have been used as banners or wrappers for religious texts. whilst silk textiles travelled west from china, buddhism entered china from india in this way. camels and horses were used as pack animals and merchants passed the goods from oasis to oasis. this textile was brought back from central asia by the explorer and archaeologist sir marc aurel stein (1862-1943). the most notable item traded was silk. the silk road was also important for the exchange of ideas. the caves of the thousand buddhas are named after a legend concerning a monk's dream of a thousand buddhas appearing on a cloud to one side of the valley where the caves are situated. it was recovered from cave 17 of the mogao grottoes. the shrines were carved out of the gravel conglomerate naturally occurring in the region.
描述_ZN: 到了唐代（公元618-906年），也就是这幅纺织品的年代，有一千个洞穴被装饰有宗教场景。 该圣地是中国伟大的佛教朝圣地之一，位于敦煌绿洲镇附近。 该遗址也是中亚地区的一部分，我们现在称之为丝绸之路，它是指从中国到欧洲穿越亚洲的一系列陆上贸易路线。 每个洞窟神龛的内部都绘有彩色壁画，其中有些壁画至今仍在。 莫高窟的大部分纺织品都是作为宗教书籍的旗帜或包装物。 年，当丝织品从中国西行时，佛教通过这种方式从印度进入中国。 年，骆驼和马被用作驮运动物，商人们在绿洲之间传递货物。 年，这个纺织品被探险家和考古学家Marc Aurel Stein先生（1862-1943）从中亚带回来。 年，最引人注目的贸易项目是丝绸。 年：丝绸之路对于思想的交流也很重要。 千佛洞是根据一个传说而命名的，这个传说是关于一个和尚梦见千佛出现在山谷一侧的云彩上，而千佛洞就位于这个山谷中。 是在莫高窟第17窟发现的。 这些神龛是由该地区自然形成的砾石砾石雕刻而成的。
